column1: My name's Hoagie.
column2: 我叫霍基。

column1: Does Mrs. Washington know you wear so much makeup?
column2: 華盛頓夫人知道你化這麼濃的妝嗎？

column1: Indeed.
column2: 確實。

column1: Like the sandwich?\255\003How quaint.
column2: 跟那個三明治一樣？\255\003真是古怪。

column1: One must wear makeup when one receives the phenomenal amount of media attention that I do.\255\003It's quite likely that I'll be president soon, you know.
column2: 一個人受到我這種程度的媒體關注時，是必須上妝的。\255\003你知道嗎，我很可能很快就會當上總統。

column1: Yes, I expect to be chosen president unanimously.\255\003I'm VERY well connected.
column2: 沒錯，我預期會被全票推選為總統。\255\003我的人脈非常廣。

column1: As a matter of fact, I do make use of artificial teeth.\255\003I find them to be far superior to the ordinary enamel variety.
column2: 事實上，我確實使用人造牙。\255\003我覺得它們遠優於普通的琺瑯質品種。

column1: Wow, what do you brush them with?
column2: 哇，那你用什麼刷？

column1: Don't you have a problem with splinters?
column2: 不會有木刺的問題嗎？

column1: Where could I get some of those?
column2: 我要去哪裡弄一副？

column1: My Uncle Henry has false teeth, too.
column2: 我亨利叔叔也有假牙。

column1: Well, I gotta go now.
column2: 好啦，我該走了。

column1: I use a toothbrush, much like everyone else.\255\003And a bit of wood polish, of course.
column2: 我用牙刷，跟大家一樣。\255\003當然還要抹點木器亮光蠟。

column1: Doesn't that taste awful?
column2: 那不會很難吃嗎？

column1: Don't they make a disposable kind?
column2: 沒有拋棄式的嗎？

column1: Not if you take them out, first.
column2: 先拿下來就不會。

column1: Actually, I believe the proprietor of this inn is working on something like that.
column2: 其實我相信這家客棧的老闆正在弄類似的東西。

column1: I've been to WAR, boy.\255\003No one who's heard the thunder of musket fire^\255\003^smelled the sulphur from a cannon blast^\255\003^and felt the fear in the hearts of his comrades^\255\003^is going to be bothered by a little thing like--\255\003OW!!\255\003Blast it!
column2: 我上過戰場，孩子。\255\003一個聽過火槍雷鳴^\255\003^聞過砲火硫磺^\255\003^感受過同袍心中恐懼的人^\255\003^是不會被這種小事困擾的——\255\003噢！！\255\003該死！

column1: Well, what about termites?
column2: 那白蟻呢？

column1: Well, what about woodpeckers?
column2: 那啄木鳥呢？

column1: Well, what about dry rot?
column2: 那乾腐病呢？

column1: Hardly.
column2: 才不會。

column1: They're rather expensive.\255\003Mine were custom-made for me by my good friend Paul Revere.
column2: 它們相當昂貴。\255\003我這副是我的好友保羅・列維爾為我訂製的。

column1: Didn't he ride a horse through town naked?
column2: 他不是裸體騎馬穿過鎮上嗎？

column1: Didn't he invent 3-D glasses?
column2: 他不是發明了 3D 眼鏡嗎？

column1: Doesn't he have a band or something?
column2: 他不是有個樂團之類的嗎？

column1: I believe you have him confused with someone else.
column2: 我想你把他跟別人搞混了。

column1: Fascinating, I'm sure.
column2: 真是引人入勝呢。

column1: The future of our nation.
column2: 我們國家的未來。

column1: That young couple by the stump?
column2: 樹樁旁邊那對年輕情侶？

column1: That young couple by the tree?
column2: 樹旁邊那對年輕情侶？

column1: Those outhouses?
column2: 那些茅房？

column1: A system of free enterprise and opportunity?
column2: 自由企業與機會的制度？

column1: No, no.
column2: 不，不。

column1: I was just admiring my reflection in the window.\255\003Striking, aren't I?
column2: 我只是在欣賞窗上自己的倒影。\255\003很出眾吧？

column1: There are two sides to everything, you know that, my boy?
column2: 凡事都有兩面，你知道嗎，孩子？

column1: Wow, what issue are you contemplating?
column2: 哇，你在思考什麼議題？

column1: Is it the legality of abortion?
column2: 是墮胎的合法性嗎？

column1: Is it death penalty laws?
column2: 是死刑法嗎？

column1: Is it victimless crimes?
column2: 是無被害人犯罪嗎？

column1: What do you think, is my left side better, or my right?
column2: 你覺得呢，我左臉比較好看還是右臉？

column1: Something horrible is on the rise.
column2: 有件可怕的事正在興起。

column1: Pollution?
column2: 污染？

column1: Imperialism?
column2: 帝國主義？

column1: Noise control laws?
column2: 噪音管制法？

column1: What?  What is it?
column2: 什麼？是什麼？

column1: I think I'm getting a blemish.
column2: 我好像長了顆痘子。

column1: Do you think I should be the `ecology president` or the `education president?`
column2: 你覺得我該當 `生態總統` 還是 `教育總統？`

column1: I'm a big fan of education.
column2: 我非常支持教育。

column1: I think ecology is very important.
column2: 我覺得生態非常重要。

column1: Depends on how many cherry trees you've chopped down.
column2: 那要看你砍了幾棵櫻桃樹。

column1: I think I have to go now.
column2: 我想我該走了。

column1: Really?\255\003How surprising.
column2: 真的嗎？\255\003真令人意外。

column1: Yes, of course, but what really matters is which one SOUNDS better.
column2: 是啊當然，但真正重要的是哪個「聽起來」比較好。

column1: Excellent point.
column2: 說得好。

column1: Well, I AM quite the adept tree-cutter.\255\003Men still tell tales of my youthful prowess.
column2: 我砍樹確實相當在行。\255\003至今仍有人傳頌我年輕時的英勇事蹟。

column1: Would you give me a demonstration?
column2: 能示範一次給我看嗎？

column1: I bet you've lost it.  You couldn't cut down a tree to \254\008     save your grandmother.
column2: 我看你早就不行了。你就算要救你奶奶也 \254\008     砍不倒一棵樹。

column1: I think I'll go look at some trees right now.
column2: 我想我現在就去看看樹。

column1: I don't see why I should.
column2: 我不覺得有這個必要。

column1: Lost it, have I?\255\003Why, I'd show you a thing or two, if there were a cherry tree nearby!
column2: 我不行了？\255\003哼，附近要是有棵櫻桃樹，我就露一手給你看！

column1: But as you can see, there isn't.
column2: 但你也看到了，並沒有。

column1: I only cut down CHERRY trees.\255\003Family tradition, you understand, cherries only.\255\003There's nothing out there but cedar and kumquats.
column2: 我只砍櫻桃樹。\255\003家族傳統，你懂的，只砍櫻桃。\255\003外面除了雪松和金桔什麼都沒有。

column1: Hey, tall, dark and spiffy.\255\003My name's Hoagie.
column2: 嘿，高高帥帥又體面的。\255\003我叫霍基。

column1: Well, how quaint.\255\003I am, of course, Thomas Jefferson^\255\003^noted scholar, musician, horseman^\255\003^student of the sciences, member of the bar^
column2: 真是古怪。\255\003我當然就是湯瑪斯・傑佛遜^\255\003^著名學者、音樂家、騎術高手^\255\003^科學的學徒、律師公會成員^

column1: Oh, sure, I've heard of you, dude.
column2: 喔當然，我聽過你，老兄。

column1: Yo, Tom.
column2: 唷，湯姆。

column1: Thomas.
column2: 是湯瑪斯。

column1: So how's the time capsule going?
column2: 那時空膠囊弄得怎樣了？

column1: What's in the can, Tommy?
column2: 罐子裡裝什麼，小湯？

column1: How goes the framing of the Constitution?
column2: 憲法起草得如何了？

column1: Dude, is that, like, THE Constitution?
column2: 老兄，那個是不是就是「那部」憲法？

column1: What are you guys doing in here?
column2: 你們在這裡幹嘛？

column1: How can you let Hancock suffer like that?
column2: 你怎麼能讓漢考克那樣受罪？

column1: Could you start a fire, please?
column2: 可以麻煩你生個火嗎？

column1: Has anyone ever told you you're a very snappy dresser?
column2: 有人跟你說過你穿得很有型嗎？

column1: Dude, I loved your work on the Declaration of Independence.
column2: 老兄，我超愛你在獨立宣言上的作品。

column1: Well, later, dude.
column2: 那就這樣啦，老兄。

column1: Later, bra.
column2: 回頭見，兄弟。

column1: Thomas.  My name is Thomas.\255\003And this, my chubby friend, is a time capsule^
column2: 湯瑪斯。我叫湯瑪斯。\255\003而這個，我圓潤的朋友，是時空膠囊^

column1: ^as if you didn't know^
column2: ^好像你不知道似的^

column1: ^filled with remembrances of our time to be revealed four hundred years hence.
column2: ^裡面裝滿我們這個時代的紀念物，四百年後才會開啟。

column1: Very well, now that you've provided that fine recent vintage wine.\255\003I plan to bury it this evening.
column2: 很好，既然你提供了那瓶上好的新年份葡萄酒。\255\003我打算今晚就把它埋了。

column1: I'm sorry to say that except for my log, we haven't got a thing.
column2: 很遺憾，除了我那根木頭之外，我們什麼都沒有。

column1: No one has brought me anything.\255\003I'm having some difficulty generating the proper spirit.
column2: 沒有人拿任何東西給我。\255\003我很難醞釀出應有的氣氛。

column1: We're writing the constitution for the United States.
column2: 我們在為合眾國撰寫憲法。

column1: That's it over there?
column2: 那邊那個就是嗎？

column1: Right now it's just A constitution, I'm afraid.\255\003We hit a slight creative block right after the preamble.\255\003That's why we've put up a suggestion box over there.
column2: 恐怕現在它還只是「一部」憲法。\255\003我們寫完序言就有點卡住了。\255\003所以我們在那邊放了個建議箱。

column1: It is.\255\003Now that our esteemed leader has sparked us with his brilliant vacuum suggestion, we're really rolling!
column2: 是的。\255\003自從我們敬愛的領袖用他那個絕妙的吸塵器建議點燃了我們，我們就一路順暢了！

column1: Not so well.
column2: 不太順利。

column1: We can't decide whether we should allow a free press or impose a tax.
column2: 我們決定不了該允許新聞自由還是課稅。

column1: An argument has broken out over whether we should separate church and state or legalize bingo parlors.
column2: 我們為了該政教分離還是把賓果廳合法化吵了起來。

column1: We can't even decide what font to use.
column2: 我們連要用什麼字體都決定不了。

column1: We're not sure if we should guarantee the right to bear arms, or if it will generate too many atrocious puns.
column2: 我們不確定該不該保障持有武器的權利，還是說那會衍生太多糟糕的雙關笑話。

column1: We don't know whether to call it the `Bill of Rights` or `Appendix A.`
column2: 我們不知道該叫它 `權利法案` 還是 `附錄 A。`

column1: I sure hope someone gives us a useful suggestion soon.
column2: 真希望快點有人給我們一個有用的建議。

column1: Great!\255\003George's suggestion about the vacuum cleaners really got the old creative juices flowing!
column2: 太好了！\255\003喬治那個吸塵器的建議真的讓我們的創意泉湧！

column1: In fact, we've just given ocelots the right to vote!
column2: 事實上，我們剛給了虎貓投票權！

column1: We've just finished up amendment 425, which prohibits spelunking on alternate Thursdays.
column2: 我們剛完成第 425 條修正案，禁止在隔週四從事洞穴探險。

column1: Even as we speak, Hancock's polishing up his `Single Syllable Undergarment` amendment.
column2: 就在此刻，漢考克正在潤飾他的 `單音節內衣` 修正案。

column1: In a few minutes, Washington's going to present his proposal to split the government into eight branches:\255\003Executive, judicial, legislative, bronchial, atypical, Freudian, elliptical, and extra-crispy.
column2: 再過幾分鐘，華盛頓就要提出把政府分成八權的方案：\255\003行政、司法、立法、支氣管、非典型、佛洛伊德、橢圓，還有特脆。

column1: By tomorrow we'll have finished all 9800 amendments!
column2: 到明天我們就能完成全部 9800 條修正案了！

column1: I hope they've got a good editor.
column2: 希望他們有個好編輯。

column1: I'd love to oblige you, young man, but I can't.\255\003This is the only log, and I'm saving it for posterity.
column2: 我很樂意幫你，年輕人，可惜不行。\255\003這是唯一一根木頭，我要留給後世。

column1: A real man is warmed by the fires of his spirit!\255\003You should listen to Washington relate his experiences at Valley Forge, and take heed!
column2: 真男人靠精神之火取暖！\255\003你該聽聽華盛頓講他在福吉谷的經歷，好好記著！

column1: What?  What's going to happen later?
column2: 什麼？等一下會發生什麼事？

column1: Why, yes.\255\003I studied at Virginia Coat and Technical, where I majored in collar theory.\255\003I was captain of the varsity cravat team.
column2: 那當然。\255\003我在維吉尼亞外套理工學院唸過書，主修衣領理論。\255\003我還是校隊領巾隊的隊長。

column1: Those are impressive credentials, Tom.
column2: 這資歷真了不起，湯姆。

column1: Ah, thank you.\255\003What was your favorite part?
column2: 啊，謝謝。\255\003你最喜歡哪一段？

column1: I liked the part about Prudence.
column2: 我喜歡講審慎的那段。

column1: I like those S's that look like F's.
column2: 我喜歡那些長得像 F 的 S。

column1: I liked the `We the People` part.
column2: 我喜歡 `我們人民` 那段。

column1: `Prudence, indeed, will dictate that Governments long established should--`
column2: `審慎確實會告誡我們，行之已久的政府不應——`

column1: Yeah, there's just one thing though^
column2: 對，不過有件事^

column1: Who's Prudence?
column2: 審慎是誰啊？

column1: Never mind.
column2: 沒事。

column1: That's not in the Declaration of--
column2: 那不在獨立宣言裡——

column1: Say, that's not bad.\255\003Maybe we can use it.
column2: 欸，這不錯。\255\003說不定我們可以用。

column1: Yo.
column2: 唷。
